source.title: On Language Models for Creoles
source.authors: Heather Lent; Emanuele Bugliarello; Miryam de Lhoneux; Chen Qiu; Anders Søgaard

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether model size and explicit weight-decay regularization change the relative performance of ERM and distributionally robust language-model training on creole data; this is a new NLP setting for the mapped generalization conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports intrinsic language-model metrics and downstream task scores, but does not report train-versus-test error gaps, random-label memorization, dropout, batch-size comparisons, sharpness, or memorized-example removal. Rows below capture its measured results bearing on model size and explicit regularization; cited findings from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The study compares ERM with DRO for creole language modeling, but tests none of V1–V8. Its model-size comparison does not establish zero training error or vary width beyond interpolation; its weight-decay comparison tests neither dropout nor optimizer choice. Feldman and Zhang (2020), an original source for V8, is cited as background without testing memorized-example removal.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors conclude that ERM outperforms DRO, that smaller models and increased weight decay do not explain away DRO's disadvantage, and that relative creole distributional stability may explain it. This superiority is clearest in intrinsic evaluation; downstream results are close and mixed. Stability is a proposed explanation, not an established causal result.
record.recipe_differences: Masked language modeling on creole corpora with ERM or DRO; intrinsic precision and pseudo-log-likelihood and downstream tagging/NER, rather than fitting random labels and measuring train-test error.
record.method_sensitivity: Performance varies with model size and dataset setup; the authors report no meaningful effect from tested weight-decay values. ERM generally outperforms DRO; Nigerian Pidgin downstream DRO scores are described as too close to draw concrete conclusions.

fits_no_version.finding: ERM generally outperforms DRO on intrinsic creole language-model metrics. Downstream results are mixed and close, particularly for Nigerian Pidgin.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these creole corpora and training recipes, DRO does not improve intrinsic language-model performance over ERM.

fits_no_version.finding: Across Tiny, Small, and Base BERT, ERM P@1 exceeds corresponding DRO-Language P@1: 31.31 versus 31.00, 47.39 versus 43.00, and 63.83 versus 60.40.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing BERT model size does not reverse DRO-Language's P@1 disadvantage in mixed-language Nigerian Pidgin training.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing DRO-Language weight decay from 0.01 to 0.30 leaves P@1 near 43; ERM at 0.01 reaches 47.39. The authors describe no meaningful weight-decay effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested weight-decay increases do not close DRO-Language's performance disadvantage for BERTSmall on mixed-language Nigerian Pidgin.

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Computational Natural Language Learning
record.problems: No direct train-versus-test gap or random-label memorization evaluation; results concern held-out language-model metrics and downstream tasks. Weight-decay section states no meaningful effect but provides limited displayed precision metrics; no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. The paper reports additional intrinsic metrics and task results, but these do not directly measure the claim versions' behaviors or train-test gaps; model-size and weight-decay condition results are retained as findings that fit no listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, chance-level random-label held-out accuracy, and coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Widening beyond the width required for zero training error and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, weight-decay decoupling, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and remedies for large-batch penalties.
Dropout effects, small-data and underfitting conditions, and jointly removing dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's tests/T3 classification to cites_only/T6. All retained rows fit no listed version. Table 6 contains one ERM condition, at weight decay 0.01, and four DRO-Language conditions; R9, R11, and R13 are extraction artifacts. No additional results bearing on V1–V8 are missing.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Large versus small batch training under epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and train-test gap relationship.
Effect of removing memorized training examples on test accuracy.
